body.statement: For every \(K\ge2\), the channel \(\mathsf G_K\), together with its declared causal completion, maps each binary observed-data law with \(\pi_x\in[1/3,2/3]\) into \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\), preserves the unrestricted optimal value, and appends only a parameter-free within-block treatment label. Therefore there is an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that \(R(n,d,K)\ge c\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n,d,K\).
body.justification: The parameter-free arm splitting transfers the binary hardness uniformly to every treatment-menu size and is needed for the necessity of bounded patient-group complexity.
body.gap: The accepted binary frontier stops at two treatments; this Blackwell reduction is a new many-arm transfer with constants independent of \(K\) and remains valid without an upper logging cap.
body.consumer: The joint frontier must dominate the binary sparse-group boundary in every menu regime, ruling out formulas that lose the \(d/\log(ed)\) obstruction.
